title: be + adjective (estado temporário)
definition: Be followed by an adjective to describe a temporary state or condition
example2: They are happy at the party.
example4: Describing how someone feels or appears at a specific moment
usage1: Pronúncia do verbo: /bi/ | Exceção: Não use o presente contínuo para estados permanentes (“I am being tired” ❌). Use o contínuo apenas para comportamento: “You are being silly.”

title: be + adjective (característica permanente)
definition: Be followed by an adjective to describe a permanent quality or fact
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi/ | Exceção: Para características que podem mudar, às vezes usa-se “be being + adj” para enfatizar comportamento momentâneo: “He is being cruel.”

title: be + noun (identidade)
definition: Be linking a subject to a noun that defines identity or role
example4: Expressing what or who someone/something is
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi/ | Exceção: Em contextos temporários de função, pode-se usar o contínuo: “He is being a father to that child.” (agindo como pai)

title: be + prepositional phrase (localização)
definition: Be followed by a prepositional phrase to indicate location or position
explanation: The book is on the table.
example4: Describing where someone or something is situated
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi/ | Exceção: Para ações em andamento, use o presente contínuo (“She is in the kitchen cooking” vs. “She is cooking in the kitchen”).

title: be for existência (there + be)
definition: Use of "there is/are" to express existence of something
explanation: There is a cat on the roof.
example4: Introducing new information or stating that something exists
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi/ em “there be” | Exceção: Em frases negativas e perguntas, a ordem muda: “There isn’t any milk.” “Is there a bank near here?”

title: be + -ing (presente contínuo)
definition: Be as auxiliary verb to form the present continuous tense for actions happening now
example4: Describing an action in progress at the moment of speaking
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi/ (auxiliar fraco: /bi/ ou /bə/) | Exceção: Verbos estativos geralmente não usam a forma contínua com “be” (ex.: “I am knowing” ❌).

title: be going to (futuro planejado)
definition: Be going to + verb to express a planned future action or a prediction based on evidence
explanation: I am going to study medicine.
example1: She is going to rain? (She is going to call you later.)
example2: They are going to build a new school.
example4: Talking about intentions or future events that are likely to happen
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi góin tu/ (reduzido: /bɪ gɔnə/) | Exceção: “Will” é usado para decisões espontâneas ou previsões sem evidência. “Going to” enfatiza plano ou evidência atual.

title: be able to (capacidade)
definition: Be able to + verb to express ability, often replacing "can" in different tenses
example1: She was able to finish on time.
example2: They will be able to attend.
example4: Expressing capability or possibility, especially in past or future tenses
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi êibol tu/ | Exceção: “Can” é mais comum no presente. “Be able to” é necessário para tempos verbais que “can” não tem (ex.: futuro, present perfect).

title: be supposed to (obrigação ou expectativa)
definition: Be supposed to + verb to indicate what is expected or required by rules or others
explanation: You are supposed to wear a uniform.
example1: She was supposed to call me.
example2: They are not supposed to enter here.
example4: Expressing obligation, expectation, or common belief
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi supôust tu/ | Exceção: “Should” expressa conselho, não necessariamente uma regra externa. “Be supposed to” implica que alguém ou algo estabeleceu a expectativa.

title: be about to (iminência)
definition: Be about to + verb to express that something will happen very soon
explanation: The movie is about to start.
example1: I was about to leave when you called.
example4: Describing an action that will occur in the immediate future
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi abáut tu/ | Exceção: Não use com advérbios de tempo específicos (“is about to start in 5 minutes” ❌). Já carrega a ideia de “agora”.

title: be + past participle (voz passiva)
definition: Be + past participle to form the passive voice, focusing on the action receiver
explanation: The cake was eaten by the kids.
example2: The letter will be sent tomorrow.
example4: When the subject receives the action instead of doing it
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi/ + particípio | Exceção: Em frases passivas, o agente (by...) é opcional. Use a voz ativa quando o executor for mais importante.

title: be used to (estar acostumado)
definition: Be used to + noun/gerund to express being accustomed to something
explanation: I am used to waking up early.
example1: She is not used to the heat.
example2: They were used to working long hours.
usage1: Pronúncia: /bi iúst tu/ | Exceção: Não confundir com “used to” no passado (fazia algo regularmente no passado, mas não agora). “Be used to” = estar acostumado.
